description.narrative: ASHM Health, through the Australian NGO Cooperation Program, is improving the testing and treatment of HIV and syphilis in pregnant women in Timor-Leste. The 'Supporting Triple Elimination' project is a key contributor to the 2030 targets of eliminating mother to child transmission of HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis B. The project involved moving from laboratory testing to rapid diagnostic tests at the Formosa Community Health Centre in Dili. This achieved a marked increase in testing and treatment by reducing wait times, which was a key focus area. Pre-intervention, 57 per cent of women received zero treatment for syphilis. Post-intervention, 98 per cent of women received some form of treatment and 83 per cent received adequate treatment. The project also supported training to midwives at the community health centre, resulting in an increase in hepatitis B birth dose vaccinations from 27 per cent in 2023 to 100 per cent consistently in 2024.

Oxfam’s Open the Books Project (Australian NGO Cooperation Program) is building the capacity of Timor-Leste’s disability movement and allies to undertake budget analysis and influence government policies and state budgets to better meet the needs of persons with disabilities. Advocacy efforts contributed to the government ratifying the International Convention of the Rights of People with Disability and the establishment of a formal Memorandum of Understanding between the Association for the Disabled in Timor Leste and the Ministry of Education to allocate specific funds in the 2022 budget to support people with disabilities who are currently studying at university.

The Australian NGO Cooperation Program continued to support NGOs to integrate COVID-response activities as part of the implementation of projects across a range of sectors and countries. This included reaching 1,967,951 participants across 28 countries with interactive sessions or one way messaging related to COVID-19 public health preventive measures and access to services.

description.narrative: The Australian NGO Cooperation Program supported UNICEF Australia to increase uptake of solar power across East Asia and the Pacific (EAP) through strengthened technical capacity in planning, design, and implementation of solar-powered systems. The project established the Regional Solar Technical Hub (the Hub), which supported governments, partners, and UNICEF Offices across 28 countries to ensure the correct design, installation, and operation of solar systems, thus reducing carbon emissions. ‍ In 2022-23, the Hub developed resources and organised training to build the capacity of stakeholders in the EAP region with knowledge, skills, and practical insights for implementing sustainable solar systems. The training focused on solarising the water and sanitation sector, supporting climate change mitigation and resilience. A total of 31 and 46 participants attended the training in Mongolia and Cambodia, respectively. The project showed improved knowledge of solar energy systems and application in water and sanitation sector across the EAP region.

title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: The Australian NGO Cooperation Program supported World Vision Australia ($1,406,457) to increase community resilience to the impacts of climate change in Timor-Leste. With 70 percent of the population reliant on rain-fed subsistence agriculture, communities in Timor Leste were empowered to adapt to climate change by working with government and local partners to deliver interventions in disaster risk reduction, climate-smart agriculture, and livelihoods (e.g., gender-equitable household decision-making and workload distribution between couples). ‍ The 2023 mid-term review showed that, of the 791 farmers trained in climate-smart agriculture, 49 percent had adopted at least one new technique. Post-training incomes also increased, with 245 households increasing their incomes on average by $11 to $20 per month after selling vegetables grown from project seeds. The project showed increased livelihood and employment opportunities that are climate-resilient and nutrition-sensitive, and increased access to financial services, especially for women and people with disability.

The Australian NGO Cooperation Program supported the Adventist Development Relief Agency to improve marketable food production in Viqueque Municipality through the establishment of kitchen gardens and water systems. The 2022 evaluation shows 62 kitchen garden owners sold an average of 72.5kg vegetables in the previous month. Kitchen gardeners also increased the number of vegetable types planted (39%) and sold (43%). The dietary diversity of participants increased from 3.9 to 4.7 food groups consumed. The project promoted composting, natural pest management techniques and the installation of small-scale irrigation systems to increase resilience to climate and seasonal variability.

title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: The Australian NGO Cooperation Program supported the Kyeema Foundation to increase community resilience to the impacts of climate change in Papua New Guinea (PNG) through various livelihood initiatives. Coral reef fisheries, which contribute substantially to food and livelihood security of coastal communities, have shown rapid decline due to increased fishing pressure and climate change. The project supported communities in PNG to adapt by introducing village chickens and vegetable gardens as alternative food sources and supporting local environmental stability through village-led coral gardening activities. ‍ Performance reporting in 2022 showed that farmers were maintaining average flocks of 50-150 birds and reported an increase of household egg consumption and village chicken sales. Ecological data showed women and youth engagement in marine conservation activities, such as mangrove restoration. The community-based approach has shown to be a successful model for building climate resilience in PNG through nature-based solutions that conserve and restore natural ecosystems.

The Australian NGO Cooperation Program, through Interplast Australia & New Zealand, supported a research project to develop, for the first time, a comprehensive evidence base on the current state of plastic and reconstructive surgery and related services across seven Pacific Island countries. This medical specialty plays a significant role in restoring function for people affected by burns, tumours, hand and foot injuries and congenital abnormalities. The recommendations of the report will be used by national governments and their health ministries to inform workforce development and planning, clinical capacity requirements and broader health system planning.

The Leprosy Mission Australia’s project Improved Leprosy Services in Timor Leste (Australian NGO Cooperation Program) is partnering with the Ministry of Health to deliver the National Leprosy Control Program in high leprosy endemic and at-risk districts. Outcomes in 2022-23 showed that 94 percent health facilities in the targeted municipalities of Manatuto and Bacau each have two trained staff with minimum standards in leprosy clinical management, 67 percent of health centres have regular accurate leprosy reports submitted to municipality health services and 100 percent of targeted municipality health services and health centres are receiving adequate supplies of leprosy multi-drug therapy. In 2022-23, the project also trained local civil society organisations in the Manatuto municipality to facilitate leprosy awareness activities and community groups to use the new global tool, National Inclusion Score Card survey to assess the level of inclusion of people with leprosy in the community.

Through the Australian NGO Cooperation Program MSI Reproductive Choices is working in Nepal to sustainably overcome the barriers to comprehensive sexual and reproductive health services among remote, poor, and marginalised communities by working closely with local governments through the establishment of public-private partnerships to make quality services accessible. An end term evaluation conducted in 2023 found that over three years (2020-2023) the project improved government service delivery and delivered 56,206 Couple Years of Protection, averting an estimated 15,382 unintended pregnancies and 10 maternal deaths. Through private sector engagement, the project also engaged 38 pharmacies from seven districts to sustainably increase access to family planning services by referring 500 clients to MS Ladies (community health workers) for relevant services.

UNICEF Australia, through the Australian NGO Cooperation Program, is improving prevention of and response to violence, abuse, exploitation, and neglect of children in Timor Leste by strengthening the country’s child and family welfare system. Key focus areas include strengthening the legal and policy framework, building the capacity of the social welfare workforce, and supporting communities to prevent and respond to violence against children. Through the leading support of UNICEF Australia, the Law on the Protection of Children and Youth in Danger was approved by the National Parliament in February 2023. This is the first Law in the history of Timor Leste specifically providing legal protection for children from all forms of violence and promoting their well-being. Other key achievements in 2022-23 included revision of eight existing Ministry of Social Solidarity and Inclusion social welfare training curricula and competency to Australian qualification standards and development of training and assessment tools.
